selection_method: Illustrative unique class examples matching the user-listed observations. No fleet means, rankings, missing-as-zero substitutions or unrequested drivers. Preserve native units per panel or use explicitly dimensionless normalization.

slides.title: Off-road capital costs reflect a new cost and service-output basis
slides.bar_method: Use separate freight/passenger panels for native-unit bars. A explicitly labeled percentage-change chart is an alternative; do not put unlike native units on a shared axis.
slides.driver_text: Reported driver: OEO replaced by CIMS capital costs normalized to service-output units; aircraft service output is derived from FAA operational data.
caveats: 2025 technology vintages. Distinct examples, no class means or ranking.

slides.title: Road-cost differences are larger for the truck examples
slides.bar_method: Paired native bars; $M 2020CAD/thousand vehicles. Select car, light truck, diesel MDV and diesel or BEV HDV; retain gasoline MDV in the table.
slides.driver_text: Reported driver: ATB retail prices divided by the 1.5 markup should largely preserve the cost basis, leaving aggregation weights as the expected main source of differences. The larger regional/long-haul aggregation change is a hypothesis for heavy trucks. ATB lacks gasoline MDV inputs present in legacy Islam et al. 2023 evidence.
caveats: The heavy-truck explanation is a hypothesis, not a verified quantitative attribution.

Gasoline MDV has a new SQLite row; it is not a missing-output example. New gasoline and diesel MDV investment costs are identical: 41.288421469437736. Keep missing source input coverage distinct from output coverage.

slides.title: Off-road operating costs follow revised capital costs and FAA aircraft evidence
slides.bar_method: Native bars with separate unit panels and, if needed, separate scales by mode so that marine legacy values remain visible. Avoid one enormous percentage axis driven by marine.
slides.driver_text: Reported method: off-road operating costs apply OEO capital-to-operating relationships to revised capital costs; aircraft use FAA-derived operating costs.
caveats: Do not claim the same final capex/opex ratio alone explains marine magnitudes. For marine MDO, capex changes by +656.55% and opex by +22238.19%. Candidate opex/capex=0.05, legacy=0.001693; the outputs do not establish a common ratio.
The requested driver can be described as a reported method, without adding an unrequested root cause or a full quantitative decomposition.

slides.title: Road operating costs now come from formulas
slides.bar_method: Separate passenger and freight panels, each with paired native bars. All rows use vintage=period=2025.
slides.driver_text: Reported driver: formula-derived costs replace costs read directly from the BEAN model.
caveats: These are examples of the requested road group, not powertrain- or fleet-weighted class averages.

slides.title: Marine freight demand is much lower in the new baseline
slides.bar_method: Paired native bars in bn tonne-km.
slides.driver_text: Reported driver: the large change in marine energy use between CEUD editions.
caveats: 2025 model-period demand; labels must say model period. Snapshot maps this model period to the 2030 demand input year.

slides.title: Other demand paths are rebased from 2019 to 2023
slides.bar_method: Choose a small explicit set (e.g. cars, passenger light trucks, school buses; heavy trucks, rail freight, medium trucks) and separate passenger/freight panels. Unselected modes need no added driver.
slides.driver_text: Reported driver: future demand is indexed to 2023 rather than the legacy 2019 demand baseline.
caveats: Different changes across modes do not imply different named drivers. Do not label 2025 modeled demand as an observed 2025 measurement.

slides.title: Bus and marine efficiencies use a different historical basis
slides.bar_method: Two panels: existing bus vintage 2020 in bn passenger-km/PJ, new marine vintage 2025 in bn tonne-km/PJ. Larger values mean more service output per unit energy.
slides.driver_text: Reported bus driver: CEUD intensities now backcast ATB values for existing stocks, replacing GREET gasoline/diesel and CNG/diesel scaling with ATB-indexed improvement. Reported marine driver: CEUD intensities and REGEN improvement assumptions replace regional-report values.
caveats: The panels intentionally use different vintage slices to illustrate the two listed observations; show both years in labels.
